"""Benchmark `rolling.rolling_sum` on a fixed batch of synthetic series.

Run as ``python bench.py [--output PATH]`` from this directory. It
times the window sums of every series with `time.perf_counter` and
prints ``PERFPROOF {"value": <seconds>}`` on stdout, so the same
command serves a ``reported`` metric (the calls alone) and a ``wall``
metric (the whole process). With ``--output`` it also saves the sums as
one ``.npy`` array of shape ``(SERIES, SAMPLES - WIDTH + 1)``, outside
the timed region, for output comparison.
"""

import argparse
import json
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from numpy.typing import NDArray

from rolling import rolling_sum

SERIES = 20
"""Number of series, one per sensor."""
SAMPLES = 100_000
"""Length of each series, in time steps."""
WIDTH = 3_000
"""Window width, in time steps."""
SEED = 20261016
"""Seed of the generator that draws the series."""


def make_series() -> list[NDArray[np.int64]]:
    """Draw the benchmark series.

    Returns
    -------
    list of numpy.ndarray of int64, each of shape (SAMPLES,)
        ``SERIES`` series of counts drawn uniformly from 0 to 999, the
        same on every run.
    """
    rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)
    return [
        rng.integers(0, 1000, SAMPLES, dtype=np.int64) for _ in range(SERIES)
    ]


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Run the benchmark once and report its time.

    Parameters
    ----------
    argv : list of str, optional
        Command-line arguments; ``sys.argv[1:]`` when omitted.

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Exit status, 0 on success.
    """
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, help="save the sums here")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    batch = make_series()
    start = time.perf_counter()
    sums = [rolling_sum(series, WIDTH) for series in batch]
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
    if args.output is not None:
        output: Path = args.output
        output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        np.save(output, np.stack(sums))
    sys.stdout.write(f"PERFPROOF {json.dumps({'value': elapsed})}\n")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

1	# Writing the benchmark spec
2	
3	perfproof measures one command, the benchmark, and checks one test
4	command. You write both into a JSON spec and lock it with
5	`perfproof bench define <name> --spec <file> --json`. Locking records the
6	hashes of the files listed in `harness`, `oracle`, `inputs` and
7	`config`, so a later change that edits them is refused.
8	
9	Keep the spec file in `.perfproof/specs/<name>.json`. Show the user the
10	command, the test command and what is compared, in one short paragraph,
11	before you lock it.
12	
13	## Choosing the benchmark
14	
15	- It runs the code the user cares about, the way it is really used, on
16	  realistic input. Not a microbenchmark of one line.
17	- One run is long enough to be far above the timer's step, and short
18	  enough that dozens of runs fit in the time the user will wait. Tell
19	  the user the expected total before you start.
20	- It is deterministic: fixed seeds, fixed input files, no network.
21	- If the code under test has its own timing, have the benchmark print
22	  one line `PERFPROOF {"value": <seconds>}` on stdout and use the
23	  `reported` metric. That times only the work, not interpreter start-up.
24	  Otherwise use `wall`.
25	
26	## Where the benchmark lives
27	
28	The baseline is a fresh checkout of the commit, so a file you wrote and
29	did not commit is not in it. Put a benchmark you wrote under
30	`.perfproof/harness/` (for example `.perfproof/harness/bench_x.py`) and
31	list it in `harness`. perfproof copies that directory, byte for byte,
32	into both versions before anything runs, and a change cannot touch it.
33	Once one file there is listed, every file in the directory is locked,
34	so put helper modules beside the benchmark and expect an edit to any of
35	them after locking to be refused. Only `.git` and `__pycache__` are
36	ignored: any other file that appears or changes there after the freeze
37	(a cache the benchmark writes beside itself, a `.DS_Store`) fails the
38	lock gate, so tell the benchmark to write caches outside that directory.
39	That includes a candidate directory the user hands you: its own
40	`.perfproof/harness/` is replaced, so keep nothing of theirs there.
41	Run it from the repository root with `cwd` `"."`.
42	
43	Do not point the command at `.venv/bin/python` or another ignored path
44	without `setup`: the baseline checkout has no such directory. Add
45	`"setup": {"commands": [["uv", "sync", "--frozen"]], "timeout_seconds":
46	600}`, which builds each version's own environment, and run the
47	benchmark with `uv run --frozen python ...` (plain `uv run` may
48	re-resolve) or `.venv/bin/python ...`, which then
49	exists in both. Never use the main checkout's environment: an editable
50	install there would import its source in both versions.
51	
52	## Choosing the checks
53	
54	- `correctness.command`: the project's tests for that code, or the whole
55	  suite if it is fast. A failing test on the new code rejects the change.
56	- `correctness.outputs`: files the benchmark writes that must be the
57	  same in both versions. Use `numbers` for numeric output (with a
58	  tolerance only if the user says results may differ slightly), `text`
59	  or `bytes` otherwise. Make the benchmark write its result to a file
60	  if it doesn't.
61	
62	## Template
63	
64	```json
65	{
66	  "schema_version": 3,
67	  "name": "<name>",
68	  "command": ["python", "bench.py", "--output", "out/result.npy"],
69	  "cwd": ".",
70	  "env": {},
71	  "metric": {"kind": "reported", "direction": "lower_is_better", "unit": "s"},
72	  "objective": "wall_time",
73	  "guardrails": [
74	    {"metric": "peak_memory", "direction": "lower_is_better", "unit": "bytes",
75	     "allowance": 0.1, "allowance_source": "default"},
76	    {"metric": "peak_gpu_memory", "direction": "lower_is_better", "unit": "bytes",
77	     "applicable": false, "reason": "no GPU is used"},
78	    {"metric": "p99_latency", "direction": "lower_is_better", "unit": "s",
79	     "applicable": false, "reason": "serves no requests"}
80	  ],
81	  "correctness": {
82	    "command": ["python", "-m", "pytest", "-q", "tests/test_thing.py"],
83	    "cwd": ".",
84	    "timeout_seconds": 300,
85	    "outputs": [{"path": "out/result.npy", "compare": "numbers"}]
86	  },
87	  "warmup": 1,
88	  "budget": {"max_rounds": 60, "max_seconds": 1800},
89	  "looks": {"n0": 10, "k": 10, "max_looks": 6},
90	  "min_effect": 0.03,
91	  "alpha": 0.05,
92	  "timeout_seconds": 120,
93	  "harness": ["bench.py"],
94	  "oracle": ["tests/test_thing.py"],
95	  "inputs": [],
96	  "config": [],
97	  "allow_runtime_change": false,
98	  "allow_cross_host": false
99	}
100	```
101	
102	## Fields worth knowing
103	
104	- `metric.kind`: `wall` (whole command), `cpu`, `reported` (the
105	  `PERFPROOF` line), `counter` (Linux only). `wall` and `cpu` are in
106	  seconds and lower is better.
107	- `guardrails`: list all three as above. Mark one `applicable: false`
108	  with a short true reason when it does not apply.
109	- `setup`: `{"commands": [[...], ...], "cwd": ".", "timeout_seconds": N}`.
110	  Argv commands run once in each version before the first run, outside
111	  the timing, with the same environment as the benchmark. It must not
112	  need credentials or a remote service.
113	- `reset`: if the benchmark changes something outside its own process
114	  (a local database, a cache directory), add
115	  `"reset": {"command": [...], "timeout_seconds": 60}` to put it back
116	  before every run.
117	- `budget` and `looks`: use the template's values (60 rounds, `n0` 10,
118	  `k` 10, `max_looks` 6), the provisional defaults the decision rule is
119	  calibrated under. Depth changes how many ideas you try, not these.
120	  `n0` and `k` must be even.
121	- `min_effect`: the bar. A change is kept only if even the low end of
122	  its range beats `1 + min_effect` (3% by default). Change it only if
123	  the user states a different bar.
124	- `harness`, `oracle`, `inputs`, `config`: the benchmark files, test
125	  files, input data and config files to lock. Paths relative to the
126	  repository. Those under `.perfproof/harness/` are installed in both
127	  versions by perfproof. Never lock the code you are trying to speed
128	  up: a change to a locked file is refused, so the change could never
129	  be measured.
130	
131	If `bench define` refuses the spec, its JSON `error.message` says why.
132	Fix that field; don't loosen a check to get past it.
133
